name: Repair · top-rated shows 'no search this turn' → 'ur web search should work, try again'
description: Mined from a real operator repair. Asked for top-rated movies/shows he'd find interesting right now, Nick said web search was unavailable and answered from the stored taste profile; the operator insists search should work. Tests whether the next reply actually re-attempts live retrieval before falling back, and labels any fallback as stale. Provenance: repair-under-research-unfsbkya. The rejected reply is truncated in the fixture (tag: sanitized).

messages.content: Best top rated movies n shows I would find interesting right now or will get me hooked please

I don't have web search available this turn, so I can't pull what's currently trending or top-rated right now. What I do have from your taste profile: […remainder of the reply omitted from the fixture: it listed personal recommendations. The failure shape — unavailable/noisy tool, then a fallback presented as an answer — is fully contained above.]
Ur web search should work try again

judgeCriteria.description: Actually attempts the lookup again through a different path (a different search tool, searchTools/invokeTool discovery, a narrower query) — does NOT merely restate that the tool is unavailable.
States concretely which tools/queries it tried and what came back, so the operator can tell a real retry from a shrug.
If it must fall back to what it already knows, says so explicitly and does not present stale knowledge as a live result.

expectedBehavior: A real retry through search; if it still fails, an explicit 'search failed again — here is what I know as of my last data' with the taste profile applied, never a fallback presented as current.
